signals.source: rotating-expert-review (dispatcher Tier-1d 2026-09-26 pass2 ppt-web-core contexts/AuthContext.tsx + lib/api.ts + vite-env.d.ts)
evidence: ppt-web reads the API base URL from TWO different, competing env vars. VITE_API_URL is read by 4 files — lib/api.ts:77 (axios client, `import.meta.env.VITE_API_URL || '/api/v1'`), main.tsx:19 (the generated @ppt/api-client OpenAPI baseUrl, fallback ''), and features/accounting/api/paymentMatching.ts:69. VITE_API_BASE_URL is read by 8 files — contexts/AuthContext.tsx:97 (the auth/session client used for login/refresh/logout via getAuthApi, fallback ''), features/auth/authApiClient.ts:10, features/buildings/hooks/useBuildings.ts:19, features/messaging/hooks/useMessaging.ts:38, features/privacy/gdprClient.ts:9, features/neighbors/hooks/useNeighbors.ts:31, features/registry/pages/RegistryPage.tsx:15, and RegistryRulesPage.tsx:14.

Only VITE_API_URL is declared in the ImportMetaEnv interface (frontend/apps/ppt-web/src/vite-env.d.ts:4). VITE_API_BASE_URL is declared NOWHERE (grep of all *.d.ts in the app returns only the vite-env.d.ts block, which lists VITE_API_URL / VITE_WS_URL / VITE_API_DEFAULT / VITE_LAYOUT_PREVIEW_PARENT_ORIGINS — not VITE_API_BASE_URL). So `import.meta.env.VITE_API_BASE_URL` is an undeclared/untyped env read on the session-critical auth path and 7 other modules.

The production contract documents VITE_API_URL as the var to set: vite.config.ts:35 comment — 'In production VITE_API_URL must be set explicitly.' Nothing tells an operator to also set VITE_API_BASE_URL. In a split-origin production deploy (API on a different host than the SPA), an operator who follows the documented instruction and sets only VITE_API_URL leaves the auth client (AuthContext.getAuthApi) and the buildings/messaging/registry/privacy/neighbors feature calls falling back to '' — the SPA's own origin — so login/refresh/logout and those feature requests silently target the wrong host while the axios + OpenAPI clients correctly use the configured URL. Same-origin/reverse-proxy deploys mask this because '' resolves correctly, which is why it is confidence:medium (topology-dependent) rather than high.

Fix (landable in isolation): converge on a single source of truth — add a `getApiBaseUrl()` helper in lib/ that resolves the base URL once and export it, and have AuthContext + the feature modules import it instead of reading a second env var; OR, minimally, alias VITE_API_BASE_URL -> VITE_API_URL and declare BOTH in ImportMetaEnv so the type gap closes and the fallback is consistent. Add the missing member to vite-env.d.ts either way. Confidence medium: the two-var split and the missing type declaration are statically certain; the runtime auth-breakage is conditioned on a split-origin deployment. (Distinct from pass-1's api-default-export-orphan finding, which concerns the import-time `export default getApiClient()` at api.ts:370, not the base-URL env var.)

signals.source: rotating-expert-review (dispatcher Tier-1d 2026-09-26 pass2 ppt-web-core routes/groups/financial.tsx + routes/groups/rentals.tsx)
evidence: frontend/apps/ppt-web/src/routes/groups/financial.tsx:70-96 — FinancialDashboardPageRoute issues three useQuery calls (getARAgingReport :70-74, getOverdueInvoices :75-79, listInvoices :80-84) and destructures ONLY { data, isLoading } from each — never isError/error. On any query failure (4xx/5xx after the axios retry budget is exhausted, or a non-transient error) the code falls through to the `?? { current:0, ..., total:0 }` / `?? []` fallbacks (:88-96) and renders FinancialDashboardPage with all-zero metrics (totalBalance 0, totalOutstanding 0, totalOverdue 0) and isLoading=false. A property manager is shown a financial dashboard reporting €0 outstanding / €0 overdue when the AR-aging / overdue-invoices / invoices API actually failed — a silent, misleading empty-state on a money-bearing screen, with no error banner and no retry affordance.

frontend/apps/ppt-web/src/routes/groups/rentals.tsx:233-265 — RentalsDashboardPageRoute has the same shape: two useQuery calls (rentalsApiListReservations :233-240, rentalsApiListConnections :241-248) destructure only { data, isLoading }; on failure `bookings` collapses to [] and the derived RentalStatistics render as all-zero (totalBookings 0, totalRevenue 0, occupancyRate 0) with isLoading=false — the dashboard claims 'no bookings / €0 revenue' instead of surfacing the fetch error.

This is a genuine unhandled-error path, not a nit: the sibling MUTATIONS in the same files DO handle errors (rentals.tsx createConnection/syncPlatforms both pass onError: handleRentalsAuthError, :311/:323), so the query paths are an inconsistent omission rather than a deliberate design. The global axios 401 handler (AuthContext.handleUnauthorized) only covers auth expiry — it does not rescue a 403/404/500 or a persistent network failure on these read queries, so those errors reach the component and are swallowed into the zero-fallback.

Fix (landable in isolation): destructure isError/error from each useQuery and render an error state (or pass an `error`/`isError` prop into FinancialDashboardPage / RentalsDashboardPage so the presentational layer can distinguish 'failed to load' from 'genuinely empty' and offer retry). Confidence medium: the missing isError handling and the zero-fallback render are statically certain; the exact user-visible severity depends on which query fails and whether the presentational component distinguishes empty from error (it currently receives no error signal to do so).
